subtopics.title: Matter Is Particles — and Here Is the Evidence

questions.question: Statement three of the Kinetic Molecular Theory links temperature to:
options: The number of particles in the sample
The average kinetic energy of the particles — higher temperature, faster motion

questions.question: The smell of a peeled orange crossing a still classroom demonstrates:
options: Diffusion — particles spreading by their own random motion

questions.question: Pollen grains jittering under a microscope are evidence of invisible particles because the grains:
options: Are far too large to move themselves — they are being bombarded unevenly by unseen water particles

questions.question: Heat and temperature differ in that:
options: Heat is energy transferred due to a temperature difference; temperature measures average kinetic energy
They are two words for the same quantity
Heat can only flow in solids

subtopics.title: Solid, Liquid and Gas in the Kinetic Molecular Theory

questions.question: In a solid, the particles:
options: Vibrate about fixed positions in a regular lattice held by strong forces

questions.question: A liquid keeps its volume but not its shape because its particles:
options: Are far apart with negligible forces
Stay close together but slide past one another

questions.question: Gases compress easily because:
options: Gas particles are soft and squash
The forces between gas particles are strong
Gas particles stop moving under pressure
Most of a gas's volume is empty space between far-apart particles

questions.question: The state a substance occupies is decided by:
options: The contest between the particles' kinetic energy and the attractive forces between them
The number of electrons per atom
The size of the container alone

subtopics.title: The Six Changes of State and the Energy They Need

questions.question: Sublimation and deposition are, respectively:
options: Liquid to gas, and gas to liquid
Solid straight to gas, and gas straight to solid — the liquid skipped both ways
Solid to liquid, and liquid to solid

questions.question: The three endothermic changes are:
options: Melting, evaporation, sublimation — all moving toward weaker forces and more freedom

questions.question: The boiling point is the temperature at which:
options: The first surface particle escapes the liquid
The liquid begins to feel hot
The thermometer reads exactly one hundred anywhere on Earth
The liquid changes to gas throughout, its vapour pressure equalling atmospheric pressure

questions.question: Water boils at about ninety-five degrees in Johannesburg because:
options: Atmospheric pressure is lower at altitude, so the vapour pressure matches it sooner

subtopics.title: Reading a Heating Curve — Why the Temperature Stops Rising

questions.question: During the plateau at zero degrees, the sample contains:
options: Ice and liquid water together, with the temperature pinned while any ice remains

questions.question: The temperature stops rising during a plateau because the supplied energy:
options: Overcomes the forces between particles, raising potential energy rather than kinetic energy
Is destroyed by the change of state

questions.question: The boiling plateau is much longer than the melting plateau because:
options: The thermometer responds slowly near one hundred
Separating liquid particles completely into gas takes far more energy than loosening a lattice into liquid

questions.question: Converting between scales: one hundred degrees Celsius is:
options: 373 kelvin — add 273 to the Celsius reading

subtopics.title: The Assembly, the Crowd and the Open Field

questions.question: The assembly rows — fidgeting on the spot, keeping shape — picture a:
options: Solid: fixed places, fixed shape, particles vibrating where they stand

questions.question: The corridor crowd — packed but sliding past each other — pictures a liquid because:
options: The people move in straight lines
It stays close-packed while flowing into the shape of its container

questions.question: Which picture you are in is decided by:
options: The tug-of-war between the particles' jiggle and their mutual pull

subtopics.title: Why the Pot Sticks at One Hundred

questions.question: The pot sticks at one hundred because the stove's energy is:
options: Being spent breaking the grips between particles, not speeding them up

questions.question: In the debt picture, the temperature climbs again only when:
options: The debt collector goes home early
The separation debt is fully paid — the last particle grips broken

questions.question: A steam burn is worse than a boiling-water splash because condensing steam:
options: Is hotter than one hundred degrees
Dumps its whole separation energy into your skin as the particles re-grip

questions.question: The staircase graph of the full journey shows:
options: A short flat step at zero and a long one at one hundred
One long flat step at fifty degrees

subtopics.title: Six Words for Changing, and the Traps That Cost Marks

questions.question: Frost forming on grass overnight, with no rain, is:
options: Deposition — water vapour becoming solid where it lands, skipping the liquid

questions.question: The one-question energy sort asks:
options: Is the substance hot or cold?
Is the change fast or slow?
Am I loosening the grip — energy in — or tightening it — energy out?
Is the substance pure or a mixture?

questions.question: Trap two warns that a cup and a bathtub of boiling water:
options: Cannot both be at the boiling point
Sit at the same temperature while the bathtub holds far more heat

questions.question: Washing drying on the line at twenty degrees shows that:
options: Evaporation happens at any temperature, from the surface only
Boiling can happen at twenty degrees
Wind raises the water's boiling point
